The system prompt does NOT vary by provider — Otterpace's coaching and safety rules are the product, and the provider only changes which model generates the words. Normalizes every provider's reply into one LlmResult: json, refusal, unusable (text arrived but was not parseable, so the caller degrades gracefully because the key was already billed), or empty (no text at all, an upstream fault the caller treats as a failed call).
name: complete

description: Anthropic branch of the LLM router: calls the Messages API through the official SDK with a json_schema output format, and normalizes the reply into an LlmResult. A refusal stop_reason becomes `refusal`, a missing text block becomes `empty` (an upstream fault), and unparseable text becomes `unusable` (the key was billed, so the caller degrades rather than erroring).
name: completeAnthropic

description: Gemini branch of the LLM router: generateContent over plain fetch. Gemini has no system role, so the coach prompt goes in systemInstruction, and its message roles differ - the assistant is called `model`. A blocked generation arrives as a finishReason on a 200 rather than an error status, so SAFETY and PROHIBITED_CONTENT map to the refusal result.
name: completeGemini

description: OpenAI branch of the LLM router: Chat Completions over plain fetch with a strict json_schema response_format and the key as a bearer token. Reached without the SDK because it is one request shape and every extra dependency is weight in a serverless bundle. A strict-schema refusal arrives in its own `refusal` field with null content, which maps to the refusal result.
name: completeOpenAI

description: Whether a provider error means the account has no credits left, as opposed to a transient burst limit. Matches the provider's own type/code first, then falls back to prose ('no credits remaining', 'credit balance is too low', 'quota exceeded') for providers that classify it only in the message. Telling someone with an empty balance to 'try again shortly' is advice that can never work, which is what this exists to prevent.

description: The sentence explaining which key a coach-backed feature needs, derived from the connected provider rather than restated per call site. With a provider it names that provider and no other, so the copy can never contradict the request the sheet is about to make; with none it offers every supported provider.
